provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Balancing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what balancing means.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate balancing on one leg.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about different body parts.
Today we will learn how to balance our bodies.

Content:
Balancing means keeping your body steady.
Stand on one foot without falling.
Walk on a straight line like a tightrope walker.
Use your arms to help you balance.

Class activity:
Children will take turns balancing on one leg.
Count how many seconds each child can balance.

Evaluation questions:
What does balancing mean?
Show me how to balance on one leg.
How can you help yourself balance?

Summary:
We learned how to balance our bodies today.

topics.title: Skipping
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate skipping with a rope.
The pupils should be able to skip in pairs with a friend.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about balancing.
Today we will learn how to skip with a rope.

Content:
Skipping means jumping over a rope.
Hold the rope with both hands.
Turn the rope and jump over it.
Skip in pairs with a friend taking turns.

Class activity:
Children will practice skipping with ropes.
Then they will work in pairs to skip together.

Evaluation questions:
How do you hold a skipping rope?
Show me how to skip.
What do you do when skipping with a friend?

Summary:
We learned how to skip with ropes today.

topics.title: Hopping
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to hop on one foot.
The pupils should be able to participate in a hopping race.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about skipping.
Today we will learn how to hop on one foot.

Content:
Hopping means jumping on one foot.
Stand on one foot and jump up and down.
Keep your foot on the ground between jumps.
Hop races are fun games where we hop to a finish line.

Class activity:
Children will practice hopping on one foot.
Then we will have a hopping race across the playground.

Evaluation questions:
What does hopping mean?
Show me how to hop on one foot.
How do we play hopping races?

Summary:
We learned how to hop on one foot today.

topics.title: Ball games: rolling
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to roll a ball to a friend.
The pupils should be able to stop a rolling ball.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about hopping.
Today we will learn how to roll balls.

Content:
Rolling means making a ball move on the ground.
Use your hands to push the ball forward.
Roll the ball to a friend who will catch it.
Stop a rolling ball by putting your foot on it.

Class activity:
Children will stand in pairs and roll balls to each other.
Then we will practice stopping rolling balls.

Evaluation questions:
How do you roll a ball?
Show me how to stop a rolling ball.
Why do we play ball rolling games?

Summary:
We learned how to roll and stop balls today.

topics.title: Ball games: bouncing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to bounce and catch a ball.
The pupils should be able to count the number of bounces.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about rolling balls.
Today we will learn how to bounce balls.

Content:
Bouncing means making a ball hit the ground and come back up.
Hold the ball and let it bounce on the ground.
Catch the ball after it bounces.
Count how many times you can bounce the ball without dropping it.

Class activity:
Children will practice bouncing and catching balls.
Then we will count how many bounces each child can do.

Evaluation questions:
How do you bounce a ball?
Show me how to catch a bouncing ball.
How many bounces can you count?

Summary:
We learned how to bounce and catch balls today.

topics.title: Animal movements
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to hop like a frog.
The pupils should be able to walk like a crab.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about bouncing balls.
Today we will learn how animals move.

Content:
Frogs hop on their two back legs.
Crouch down and hop forward like a frog.
Crabs walk sideways on their hands and feet.
Get on your hands and feet and move sideways like a crab.

Class activity:
Children will take turns hopping like a frog.
Then they will practice walking like a crab across the floor.

Evaluation questions:
How does a frog move?
Show me how to hop like a frog.
How does a crab walk?

Summary:
We learned how to move like animals today.

topics.title: Health: food and growth
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list good foods.
The pupils should be able to explain why good food helps us grow.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about animal movements.
Today we will learn about food and growth.

Content:
Good food helps our bodies grow strong.
Rice, beans, plantain and fish are good foods.
Fruits like oranges and bananas are also good.
Eat good food to grow tall and healthy.

Class activity:
Children will draw pictures of good foods they eat.
Then they will share what helps them grow strong.

Evaluation questions:
Name some good foods.
Why do we need good food?
How does good food help us grow?

Summary:
We learned that good food helps us grow strong.

topics.title: Rest and sleep
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why rest is important.
The pupils should be able to state when to sleep early.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about food and growth.
Today we will learn about rest and sleep.

Content:
Rest means taking a break from playing or work.
Rest helps our bodies feel strong again.
Sleep early at night to rest well.
Good sleep helps us grow and learn better.

Class activity:
Children will pretend to rest for one minute.
Then they will share what they do to rest at home.

Evaluation questions:
Why do we need to rest?
When should we sleep?
How does sleep help us?

Summary:
We learned why rest and sleep are important.

topics.title: Relay games
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to run and pass a baton.
The pupils should be able to participate in team games.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about rest and sleep.
Today we will learn about relay games.

Content:
Relay games are team games where we run and pass objects.
Run to a friend and give them the baton.
The next person runs and passes it back.
Work together to finish the relay race.

Class activity:
Children will form teams and play relay games.
They will practice running and passing a baton.

Evaluation questions:
What is a relay game?
Show me how to pass a baton.
Why do we work together in relay games?

Summary:
We learned how to play relay games today.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to demonstrate skills learned this term.
The pupils should be able to name activities we practiced.

Introduction:
This is the last week of term.
Today we will practice all we learned.

Content:
We learned balancing, skipping and hopping.
We played ball games and moved like animals.
We learned about food, rest and sleep.
We played relay games with our friends.

Class activity:
Children will show all the skills they learned.
Each child will demonstrate their favorite activity.

Evaluation questions:
What was your favorite activity this term?
Show me how to balance.
Why is good food important?

Summary:
We practiced all we learned this term.
